statement: For every odd n at least 3 and every coefficient prime, the nontrivial procyclic subgroups of the geometric pro-prime group of the genus-n odd dihedral cover with open arithmetic normalizer are precisely the nontrivial subgroups of cusp inertia conjugates. A general compact-type tame monodromy argument shows that a normalized nonzero proper homology class cannot be supported on two positive-genus components.

Rational conjugator normalization is used only for a necessary equation, never to lift a rational element integrally or split a normalizer extension. The two-block quotient kills both the candidate homology vector and the surface relation, while monodromy has coefficient equal to the strictly positive distance between the two components. Each actual odd-family component map is the identity followed by [1+i], hence injective on rational homology at every odd coefficient prime. A.46 treats coefficient two.
